ashok: quick heads-up — bringup for rbk3b-int8 shows a repeatable quality dip on short queries (<= 6 tokens) in our rerank bench. NDCG@10 and MRR both down vs float32. attaching short summary below. :thinking:

maria: ack, can you paste the exact eval command + quant config?

ashok: yup — run: ```./eval/run_rerank.sh --model rbk3b --quant int8 --seed 42 --holdout shortqueries --batch 128 --prompt-type primed```
quant config: ```bits=8; per_channel=true; clip=0.15; kvpack=false```

devin: can you paste the metric delta? numbers help triage.

ashok: summary table from the latest CI run: ```
metric         | float32  | int8     | delta
NDCG@10        | 0.781    | 0.742    | -0.039
MRR            | 0.612    | 0.589    | -0.023
Top1 accuracy  | 0.483    | 0.461    | -0.022
```
these are pooled across holdout; short-query slice is worse: NDCG drop ~ -0.06.

maria: interesting. any difference in tokenization or priming between float and quant runs? same docker image?

ashok: same container image, same tokenizer artifact. we do one extra priming token in the short-query harness (legacy priming). suspect mismatch in how kv cache pack interacts with short sequences during generation scoring.

devin: kvpack=false in config — but runtime still used a cached path earlier? can you paste the runtime flags from the serving job?

ashok: runtime flags from CI:
```
--use_kvcache=true --kvpack_enabled=false --prefetch_prefix=false --batching=adaptive
```
so kvcache still on.

sophia: suggestion — run three ablations: (A) float32 baseline replica with same runtime flags, (B) int8 with kvcache disabled, (C) int8 but remove priming token. that should isolate whether priming vs kvcache vs quantization is the main factor.

ashok: starting (A)-(C) now. queuing jobs in eval pool. ETA ~ 25m.

eval-bot: job 1769743220 triggered: rerank-ablation-A (float32 runtime-parity) started on runner-eval-7. link: https://ci.redwood/tests/1769743220 :robot_face:

maria: one more thought — we recently landed a tokenizer micro-change that strips trailing newline for short queries in prod harness. double-check the preprocess pipeline — if float run used preproc with strip_newline but int8 run used older artifact, that could shift token lengths and attention patterns.

ashok: good call. verifying pipeline artifacts. current runs are using artifact v2026-03-18. float/aggressive vs quant/legacy mapping looked consistent but i'll confirm.

devin: also capture logits on a small sample to see if quant induces calibration shift (softmax temperature changes). small dump of topk logits can be very telling.

ashok: will capture topk logits for 50 samples from the short-slice run. planning a diff like: ```python tools/compare_logits.py --ref float32.dump --cand int8.dump --k 5```

eval-bot: job 1769743235 triggered: rerank-ablation-B (int8 kvcache-off) started on runner-eval-3.

ashok: quick intermediate update — (A) float32 replica finished: metrics match previous baseline within noise (ndcg 0.782). (B) int8 kvcache-off finished: ndcg@10=0.760 (still -0.022 vs float). (C) int8 remove-priming finished: ndcg@10=0.780 (almost parity).

maria: oh that is super informative — removing the priming token recovered the signal for int8. so priming+quant seems to interact badly.

devin: possible explanations: priming token causes a very short prefix attention pattern that, after quantization, produces a shifted softmax in early positions which cascades. or quant rounding in the first kv writes creates misalignments.

ashok: captured logits diff for 50 samples. quick grep shows larger early-token logit variance for int8 with priming present. sharing snippet: ```
sample 12: float top1 logits: [3.12, 2.01, 1.45]
           int8+prim top1 logits: [2.89, 1.52, 1.03]
diff early mean: -0.18
```

sophia: ok action items: 1) short-term: disable priming for int8 model in rollout or use priming only in float path; 2) medium: run quantization sweep with alternative clipping (try clip=0.2, asymmetric) and per_token_bias_correction; 3) long-term: add a unit test in eval harness that checks priming/shortquery slice across quant configs.

maria: also file a ticket to check whether prefix-cache write/read rounding is using same dtype path — if reads are cast to float32 but writes truncated in int8 variant we will see non-deterministic drift.

ashok: creating ticket INF-2317 with the triage notes and attaching logs/dumps. tagging infra and runtime.

devin: for immediate rolling: if we have a canary rule that routes short-query traffic to float32 or to int8-without-priming, do that. safer than rollback.

ashok: agree. i'll propose traffic rule: short_query_len<=6 -> int8_no_priming fallback to float32 if latency within SLA. posting canary config PR soon.

maria: great work. thanks for the quick ablation and logs. :thumbsup:

ashok: thanks all — will update thread with PR link and ticket once done.
